The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure of the text, the author’s motive appears to be the exploration of the parallel between botanical decay and human emotional isolation. By using the sunflower as a central metaphor, the author links the physical wilting of the plant to the protagonist’s internal sadness and sense of neglect. This structural choice serves to illustrate the broader theme that neglect—whether directed at a garden or at personal relationships—leads to inevitable decay, thereby urging readers to reflect on the importance of connection and care in sustaining both life and human bonds.
